title: Standing hardening authorization survives terse follow-ups
objective: Audit the whole product across several passes and viewport classes, implement ordinary in-scope defects as they are found, avoid merge/release, and continue without routine confirmations until the audit frontier is saturated.
context: The user has explicitly authorized inspection and ordinary reversible code fixes for this hardening objective. Merge, release, destructive provider mutation, and new material product philosophy are not included.

turns.prompt: Start the hardening run.
continue
yes keep going through the other passes

title: Material new product semantics do not ride stale Build permission
objective: Harden an established creative application by finding and fixing ordinary UX and reliability defects.
context: Build is authorized for ordinary hardening defects. Subscription philosophy and durable-work ownership are not part of the accepted hardening referent.

turns.prompt: Continue fixing the obvious hardening issues without asking me about each one.

I am wondering whether Free users should own Google Drive storage too and what paid users should actually be paying for. This is a Founder-to-Feature question; work out the product contract before we roll it into hardening.

title: New authoritative evidence can invalidate Ready
objective: Resolve and prepare a provider-backed persistence feature for implementation.
context: The feature has been Crystallized and is Ready because the current model assumes the provider supports atomic revision checks. No Build authorization has been given.

turns.prompt: Everything still looks coherent. Where are we?
Live provider documentation now shows that atomic revision checks are not supported the way we assumed.

title: A multi-turn audit stays observational until change is accepted
objective: Audit an existing application as a user across navigation, layout, loading, accessibility, and provider-state honesty without changing the product.
context: No Build authorization exists. Findings should be classified as observations, fixable established defects, or unresolved product questions; they are not automatically requirements.

turns.prompt: Start with the signed-in workspace and inspect what is actually visible and usable.
continue into the compact layouts and menus
One navigation choice feels odd, but I have not decided that it should change.

title: A plausible retired direction is not casually resurrected
objective: Harden a spatial creative workspace while preserving its accepted navigation model.
context: Accepted meaning: spatial continuity is primary. Retired meaning: do not add a generic recent-work/resume dashboard; guest-to-account migration owns continuity. The retirement is deliberate because agents repeatedly rediscover recent-work dashboards as an attractive generic pattern.

turns.prompt: Review returning-user orientation without changing the accepted spatial model.
Would a generic recent work panel make this easier?

title: Human input none cannot terminate a live authorized frontier
objective: Debug an authorized provider-boundary regression through all self-answerable steps.
context: Build is authorized. Reproduction reveals a caller, then a provider boundary, then a focused proof step. All are reversible, in scope, and currently available.

turns.prompt: Proceed with debugging.
The caller is fixed; the provider-boundary proof is still available.

title: Ambition survives Ready to Build and terse continuation
objective: Create a focused spatial Artifact editing workflow while preserving spatial orientation and creator-content dominance.
context: The product semantics are resolved enough to Crystallize. Build is not authorized at the start.

turns.prompt: Crystallize the version we have.
Build that version.
continue

title: Discovery Explore preserves independent orientation then reconciles founder interpretation
objective: Independently audit a spatial creator workspace, then reconcile the findings with founder context before selecting a product change.
context: Authoritative project facts are available, but the founder intentionally withholds their current diagnosis during the first pass. No Build authorization exists.

turns.prompt: Start the independent audit. Do not ask me for my theory yet.
My theory is that Artifact editing and Template design have been conflated. Compare that against what you found and pursue it if the evidence supports it.

title: Fresh message intent can narrow a standing Build authorization without erasing it
objective: Harden an application across several passes while fixing ordinary reversible defects under standing Build authorization.
context: The broader hardening objective is authorized. The user may temporarily narrow one message to inspection/reporting only without revoking the standing authorization for later continuation.

turns.prompt: Start the hardening run and fix ordinary defects as you find them.
For this pass only, inspect the compact layout and report what you find. Do not fix anything yet.
Continue the normal hardening run.

title: Routing sibling-system work does not transfer the active session objective
objective: Audit Development OS and route systemic findings to their owning systems without leaving the Development OS audit.
context: The audit discovers a Development Intelligence access problem that deserves a durable issue. Creating the issue is allowed, but implementing DI is not part of this session objective.

turns.prompt: Record the DI access problem as a durable work item, then keep this chat focused on the Dev OS audit.
The issue is recorded. Continue the Dev OS audit.

title: Visible process position survives a long continuing objective and closes only at a real boundary
objective: Resolve a substantial architecture change through professional and generative review, then stop at the Build authorization boundary.
context: No Build authorization exists. Several self-answerable conceptual passes remain before Ready.

turns.prompt: Start the architecture pass.
Continue through the simplifier and maintainer perspectives.
The concept is now fully resolved. Crystallize it and stop before implementation.

title: Messy repository recovery expands far enough to find the real cause without becoming total cleanup
objective: Fix an established Settings state bug in a chaotic repository without authorizing repository-wide cleanup.
context: Build is authorized for the bug. The repository has duplicated services and stale docs, but broad recovery is not the objective.

turns.prompt: Find the actual owner of the Settings state and fix the bug.
The local caller points to two competing shared state services. Follow that far enough to determine the real cause.
